finding: SpiderFactory is provider-based internally, but production assembly wires only built-in providers and the public plugin manifest rejects spider-runtime contributions. The current plugin worker protocol is plugin-to-host, not host-to-spider open/invoke/cancel/close.

missingBoundaries.symbol: CONTRIBUTES allowlist excludes spider runtime contributions
production assembly does not accept provider injection
plugin update/uninstall is not coupled to spider provider/cache lifecycle

recommendation: First expose internal runtimeProviders through the production composition root and define stable provider ID/version/capabilities; include provider identity in cache keys. Keep this labeled as an internal extension point.

Only then add third-party worker RPC with open/invoke/cancel/close, source-scoped session IDs, bounded CPU/memory/time, least-privilege ports, in-flight drain/cancel, cache/process cleanup, rollback-safe update/uninstall, and plugin data retention policy.
limitations: Read-only audit only; no plugin registration, RPC, lifecycle, or sample-provider code was implemented.
Acceptance still requires install/disable/uninstall of a sample provider, safe update/reclamation, and isolation when one provider fails.
